correctness.rationale: For every color on a cubic prism, the vertex/edge incidence count gives even vertex count and a perfect matching on the complement. Three occupied consecutive rungs isolate a vertex in this complement, forcing each even vertex-class size to be at most 2 floor(m/3). Four classes sum to 2m, forcing minimum size at least 2(m mod 3) and discrepancy at most floor(m/3)-(m mod 3). Negative bound excludes m=5. The explicit four finite cyclic blocks have directly verified compatible transitions and exact class-size vectors; concatenations attain equality for all other m at least 3. Independently implemented finite transfer-state and original-graph checks pass but are not used as infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 18 and its pasting examples are weaker in the relevant quantifier: they exhibit one coloring but do not bound all colorings. The small-order all-cubic classifications in the later paper do not imply a sharp infinite function restricted to prisms. The full 1988 and 2026 documents remain a priority risk.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Extremal total-color-class discrepancy is equivalent in a cubic graph to half the spread between four even vertex-color class sizes, via s_j+2e_j=2m. Prior work contains this latter identity, so mere restatement would not be new. The new no-three-consecutive-rungs bound is needed to determine the maximum over all prism colorings and is not implied by the prior existence constructions.

value.rationale: The extremal all-coloring discrepancy is a natural quantitative refinement of recently studied non-equitability on cyclic prisms; showing that pasted witnesses exist is insufficient. The local perfect-matching isolation obstruction yields a sharp universal bound, saturated by residue-class-specific constructions. The exact result for every m reveals a linear-in-m maximum imbalance, not previously supplied by the accessible qualitative examples.
